record.paper_title: Hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin methods for second-order elliptic problems: overview, a new result and open problems
record.original_question: Construct new M-decompositions beyond the cases already developed for V_g(K) × W_g(K) = P_k(K) × P_k(K), specifically by working out the case in which a = Id and V_g(K) × W_g(K) = ∇W(K) × W(K).

evidence.quote: New M-decompositions. The known M-decompositions, see [ 27 , 28 , 55 ] and [ 30 , 54 ], have been developed for V_g(K)×W_g(K):=P_k(K)×P_k(K) only. It would be interesting to work out the case set a:=Id and V_g(K)×W_g(K):=∇W(K)×W(K).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded polyhedral domain with a conforming simplicial (or polytopal) mesh $\mathcal{T}_h=\{K\}$. For a single element $K$ with boundary $\partial K$, consider the local hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) approximation of a second–order elliptic problem written in mixed form
\[
a\,\boldsymbol q + \nabla u = 0,\qquad \nabla\!\cdot\!\boldsymbol q = f \quad\text{in }K,
\]
with numerical trace $\widehat u$ on $\partial K$. The local HDG method is defined by finite–dimensional spaces $V(K)\subset L^2(K;\mathbb{R}^d)$ for the flux $\boldsymbol q$, $W(K)\subset L^2(K)$ for the scalar variable $u$, and $M(\partial K)\subset L^2(\partial K)$ for the trace $\widehat u$.

M-decomposition. Following the standard definition, the pair $(V(K),W(K))$ is said to admit an $M$-decomposition with respect to $M(\partial K)$ if there exist subspaces $\widetilde V(K)\subset V(K)$ and $\widetilde W(K)\subset W(K)$ such that
\[
V(K) = V_g(K) \oplus \widetilde V(K),\qquad W(K) = W_g(K)\oplus \widetilde W(K),
\]
and the trace operators induce an isomorphism between $\widetilde V(K)\cdot\boldsymbol n \oplus \widetilde W(K)|_{\partial K}$ and $M(\partial K)$, where $V_g(K)\times W_g(K)$ is a prescribed "filling" pair satisfying $\nabla\!\cdot V_g(K)\subset W_g(K)$ and $\nabla W_g(K)\subset V_g(K)$ (so that the standard HDG stability and superconvergence analysis applies).

Known case. For the classical choice $V_g(K)\times W_g(K) := \mathcal{P}_k(K;\mathbb{R}^d)\times \mathcal{P}_k(K)$ (polynomials of total degree at most $k$) and the diffusion coefficient $a=\mathrm{Id}$, explicit $M$-decompositions and the corresponding minimal enrichments $\widetilde V(K),\widetilde W(K)$ have been constructed on simplices, cubes, prisms, pyramids, and certain polygonal/polytopal elements, yielding superconvergent HDG methods.

Problem. Take $a := \mathrm{Id}$ and the alternative filling pair
\[
V_g(K)\times W_g(K) := \nabla W(K)\times W(K),
\]
where $W(K)$ is a chosen finite-dimensional subspace of $H^1(K)$ (and $\nabla W(K) := \{\nabla w : w\in W(K)\}\subset L^2(K;\mathbb{R}^d)$). For this choice, construct an $M$-decomposition of $(V(K),W(K))$ with respect to a suitable trace space $M(\partial K)$. Specifically:

(i) Identify natural candidates for $W(K)$ (e.g., spaces beyond $\mathcal{P}_k(K)$, including spaces on general polytopal elements) for which such an $M$-decomposition exists.

(ii) Determine the smallest spaces $\widetilde V(K)$ and $\widetilde W(K)$ that must be added to $V_g(K)=\nabla W(K)$ and $W_g(K)=W(K)$ so that $(V(K),W(K))$ admits an $M$-decomposition with respect to $M(\partial K)$.

(iii) Prove that the resulting HDG method is well defined, stable, and superconvergent in the sense provided by the general theory of $M$-decompositions.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned the standard literature on M-decompositions for HDG methods (Cockburn–Fu and collaborators), all of which develop M-decompositions for the polynomial filling pair $\mathcal{P}_k(K)\times\mathcal{P}_k(K)$. No source was found that constructs an M-decomposition for the alternative filling pair $\nabla W(K)\times W(K)$ with $a=\mathrm{Id}$, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: An Introduction to the Theory of M-Decompositions (Cockburn)
status_evidence.snippet: M-decomposition theory provides a systematic approach to devise HDG and mixed methods proven superconvergent on unstructured meshes; existing constructions use polynomial filling pairs.
status_evidence.claim: Existing M-decomposition constructions are based on polynomial filling pairs P_k(K)×P_k(K).

status_evidence.title: An Introduction to the Theory of M-Decompositions (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style chapter on the theory of M-decompositions and superconvergent HDG methods, focusing on polynomial spaces.
status_evidence.claim: No construction with filling pair ∇W(K)×W(K) is reported in the standard surveys.
